q-11124.name: Question 1
q-11124.problem: Find where the normal line to the curve $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(1,2)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
q-11124.worked_solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{1/2}) \\  & ={x}^{-1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the slope of the tangent line is

$$
m={f}^{′}(1)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}}=1,
$$

and therefore the slope of the normal line is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-1.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-2 & =-1(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1+2 \\ y & =-x+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the $y$-axis by setting $x=0$ and solving the resulting equation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0+3 \\ y & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal line intersects the $y$-axis at  $(0,3).$

Find where the normal line to the curve f(x)=2x at the point (1,2) intersects the y-axis.

Correct
EXPLANATION

Taking the derivative, we have f′(x)=ddx(2x)=ddx(2x1/2)=x−1/2=1x.

So the slope of the tangent line is m=f′(1)=11=1, and therefore the slope of the normal line is m′=−1m=−1.

Finally, the equation of the normal line is y−2=−1(x−1)y=−x+1+2y=−x+3.

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the y-axis by setting x=0 and solving the resulting equation. We get y=−0+3y=3.

Therefore, the normal line intersects the y-axis at (0,3).

q-47406.name: Question 2
q-47406.problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2{x}^{2}$ at the point $(2,8)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $p+q.$
q-47406.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})=4x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2)=4(2)=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-8 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-2) \\ 8y-64 & =-x+2 \\ x+8y & =66.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p+q=8+66=74.$

q-342187.name: Question 3
q-342187.problem:
Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=4x-\frac{2}{x}$ at the point $(-1,-2).$

$x\,+$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
q-342187.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4x-\frac{2}{x}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-\frac{2}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-2{x}^{-1}) \\  & =4+2{x}^{-2} \\  & =4+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(-1,-2):$

$$
m={f}^{′}(-1)=4+\frac{2}{(-1)^{2}}=4+2=6
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{6}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-2) & =-\frac{1}{6}[x-(-1)] \\ -6(y+2) & =x+1 \\ -6y-12 & =x+1 \\ x+6\cdot y & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$
